name: FT Habit
classification_notes: A geometric sans that mixes smooth curves with sharp edges, pulling from early-to-mid twentieth-century models for a retro-tinted personality.
summary: A geometric sans with a fun, retro vibe, mixing smooth curves and sharp edges across six weights.
description: FT Habit blends different type styles into one family, pulling on early-to-mid twentieth-century design models to give bold headlines some character rather than pure geometric neutrality. It ships with italics across all six weights and covers 200-plus languages.
foundry_blurb: Formula Type describes FT Habit as a geometric sans serif with character that blends different styles, mixing smooth curves with sharp edges, perfect for bold headlines.

name: FT Aktual
classification_notes: A flexible modern grotesque built to work equally at large headline sizes and smaller text, in print or on screen.
summary: A flexible modern grotesque fresh and well-rounded enough for both large headlines and smaller text, in print or on screen.
description: FT Aktual runs fourteen styles across seven weights with matching italics, extending beyond Latin into Greek. Stylistic sets give it a distinct personality without compromising its workhorse range.
foundry_blurb: Formula Type describes FT Aktual as a flexible, modern grotesque, fresh, original and well-rounded, great for both large headlines and smaller text whether on screens or in print.

name: FT Supplement
classification_notes: A tall, narrow display face taking its cue from early twentieth-century wood type used in posters and newspapers.
summary: A tall, narrow display face styled on early twentieth-century wood type, built for posters, titles and standout logos.
description: FT Supplement's condensed design and tight spacing take after old wood type used in posters and newspapers, with eight stylistic sets of alternates for varying the texture across a large composition.
foundry_blurb: Formula Type describes FT Supplement as a display font that takes its cue from old wood types, its tall, narrow design and details reminiscent of early twentieth-century posters and newspapers.

name: FT Kunst Grotesk
classification_notes: A grotesque mixing 1950s typographic references with a modern digital finish, sitting between historical grotesque and contemporary neutrality.
summary: A grotesque mixing past and present, inspired by 1950s typography and finished with a modern digital feel.
description: FT Kunst Grotesk combines subtle period detail with contemporary proportions across five weights and matching italics, supporting Greek alongside its extended Latin set.
foundry_blurb: Formula Type describes FT Kunst Grotesk as a grotesque that mixes past and present, inspired by typography from the 1950s, combining subtle details with a modern digital feel.

name: FT Regola Neue
classification_notes: A friendly hybrid of geometric shapes and grotesque structure, blending 1920s and 1930s references with contemporary neo-grotesque proportions.
summary: A friendly, contemporary sans combining geometric shapes and grotesque structure across six weights with italics.
description: FT Regola Neue works well for both headlines and body text, blending elements from the 1920s and 1930s with the proportions of modern neo-grotesque design.
foundry_blurb: Formula Type describes FT Regola Neue as combining geometric shapes and grotesques to produce a friendly, contemporary style, a playful font that works well for both headlines and body text.

name: FT Speaker
classification_notes: A retro-futurist display face referencing dot-matrix and flip-dot displays, including a screen-specific monospaced variant built on a 7x7 dot grid.
summary: A retro-futurist display face recalling dot matrices and flip-dot displays, with a 7x7-grid Mono Screen variant.
description: FT Speaker's sturdy, flexible structure comes with a comprehensive stylistic set including 400 symbols and emoticons, plus a Mono Screen cut built specifically on a 7x7 dot grid for genuinely low-resolution display work.
foundry_blurb: Formula Type describes FT Speaker as a retro-futurist font inspired by digital aesthetics as well as art and design, its letters bringing to mind dot matrices and flip dot displays.

name: FT Athletic
classification_notes: A rough, distinctive display face influenced by sportswear graphics, old video-game packaging and DIY fonts, referencing ITC Machine, ITC Superstar and Berthold City.
summary: A rough, DIY-flavoured display face with the feel of old video games, masking tape and basketball matches.
description: FT Athletic draws on sportswear and college graphics, vintage video-game packaging and homemade lettering, referencing ITC Machine, ITC Superstar and Berthold City. It ships in both proportional and monospaced versions across six weights.
foundry_blurb: Formula Type describes FT Athletic as a versatile display font with the feel of old video games, masking tape and basketball matches, inspired by sportswear and college graphics.
